rationale: IMPL: with_read_inline at pool.rs:90-103 runs f(&*obj) directly on the current thread — zero spawn_blocking inside the method body, unlike with_read at pool.rs:75-88 which uses tokio::task::spawn_blocking. The sole await is get().await for pool checkout; the closure executes synchronously after that. GATE TEETH: test builds a 4-thread cap runtime (max_blocking_threads=4), spawns N=8 concurrent spawn_blocking tasks each of which block_on an inline read while sleeping 50ms to force overlap, then wraps joins in a 10s timeout so deadlock becomes Elapsed failure. REGRESSION RE-DERIVED: mutating the impl to nested spawn_blocking caused Elapsed(()) at 10.12s — identical to the orchestrator-reported failure. Revert verified by git diff --stat showing zero delta. NON-VACUOUS: test asserts counts.len()==8 and every element==2 (both written nodes visible), so a no-op impl cannot pass.
